name: Machinist
author: CalcShelf
description: Shop tools for machinists: speeds and feeds, thread pitch and tap drills, number, letter, fractional and metric drills with their metric and inch sizes, clearance holes, shop calculators, and a G-code and M-code reference.

items.title: Spindle speed for a material
items.note: The middle of the starting range in the cutting-speed table. Adjust for the tool maker’s data, rigidity and coolant.

items.title: Cutting speeds (starting values)
items.note: Typical starting ranges for turning and milling. Drilling usually runs at the low end and tapping lower still. Follow the tool maker’s figures where you have them.

items.title: Unified (inch) tap drills
items.note: Tap drills for about 75 % thread (Starrett chart); the last column is the thread depth that drill gives, from % = (D − drill) · TPI / 0.01299.

items.title: Metric (ISO) tap drills
items.note: Tap drills from Starrett’s chart (M8 × 1.25 uses the common 6.8 mm). % thread = (D − drill) / P × 76.98.

items.title: Pipe tap drills (NPT)
items.note: Drill sizes for tapping without reaming (Starrett chart). With a taper pipe reamer, drill one size smaller.

items.title: Tap drill for a thread percentage (inch)
items.note: Then look up the nearest drill in the Drills table. 60–75 % is usual; tough materials take less.

items.title: Tap drill for a thread percentage (metric)
Unified thread dimensions
items.note: Basic (nominal) dimensions for a 60° thread, P = 1/TPI. Tolerances by class are not included.

outputs.label: Compound infeed at 29.5° for the full external depth

items.title: Metric thread dimensions
items.note: Basic ISO dimensions (ISO 724). Tolerances by class are not included.

items.title: Three-wire thread measurement
items.note: For 60° threads. E is the pitch diameter you want; the best wire touches at the pitch line.

outputs.label: Smallest and largest wire that work

items.title: All drills by size
items.note: Number, letter, fractional (to 1 in) and metric drills together, smallest first. Type a size to see the nearest drills.

items.title: Metric drills
items.note: 0.3–10 mm in 0.1 mm steps, 10–20 mm in 0.5 mm steps, 20–32 mm in 1 mm steps.

items.title: Countersink depth
items.note: Depth from the surface to reach the countersink diameter D_c. Use d = 0 for a sharp point.

inputs.label: Diameter at the bottom (0 for a point)

items.title: Bolt circle
items.note: Hole centres, starting at angle θ₀ from the +X axis and going counter-clockwise.

inputs.label: Angle of the first hole θ₀

items.title: Canned cycle formats (mill)
items.md:
```
G81 X Y Z R F         drill
G82 X Y Z R P F       drill, dwell P at the bottom
G83 X Y Z R Q F       peck drill, peck depth Q
G73 X Y Z R Q F       chip-break peck
G84 X Y Z R F         tap; F = S × pitch
G80                   cancel
```
G98 returns to the start height between holes and G99 to the R plane. Z is the bottom of the hole and R the height where feeding starts.

items.title: A typical program start
items.md:
```
%
O1001 (PART NAME)
G20 G17 G40 G49 G80 G90   (safe start: inch, XY, cancel comp and cycles, absolute)
T1 M06                    (tool 1)
G54 G00 X0 Y0             (work offset, rapid to start)
S2000 M03                 (spindle on)
G43 H01 Z1.0 M08          (length offset, coolant)
...
M09
G91 G28 Z0                (home Z)
M30
%
```
An example only: check the safe-start line and the homing moves for your control.
